stemMd:
Consider these four events in European history:

- the Congress of Vienna, which redrew the map of Europe at the end of the Napoleonic Wars
- the proclamation of the German Empire in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles
- the storming of the Bastille in Paris
- the wave of revolutions across Europe known as the Springtime of Peoples

Which list gives them in the order in which they happened, earliest first?

options.label: A

options.label: C
options.textMd: Congress of Vienna, storming of the Bastille, Springtime of Peoples, German Empire

options.label: D
options.textMd: Storming of the Bastille, Springtime of Peoples, Congress of Vienna, German Empire

options.textMd: Storming of the Bastille, Congress of Vienna, Springtime of Peoples, German Empire

explanationMd:
**What to notice first.** You do not need four exact dates if you follow the chain of cause and effect. The French Revolution led to Napoleon; the Congress of Vienna settled Europe after him; the revolutions of 1848 rose against the order the Congress had restored; and German unification came later still, after the Franco-Prussian War - which is why it was proclaimed at Versailles, in defeated France.

**The dates that settle it.**

- Storming of the Bastille: 14 July 1789.
- Congress of Vienna: 1814-1815.
- Springtime of Peoples: 1848.
- Proclamation of the German Empire at Versailles: 18 January 1871.

So the order is the Bastille, the Congress of Vienna, the Springtime of Peoples, the German Empire.

**How to check it.** Each wrong list moves exactly one event out of place, so test the list link by link. The Bastille must come first, because the Congress and the 1848 revolutions are both consequences of the Revolution that began in 1789. The Congress must come before the Springtime of Peoples, because the 1848 revolutions rose against the order it had restored. And the German Empire must come last, because the failure of 1848 to unite Germany was only made good in 1871.

distractorRationale.d: This list puts the Springtime of Peoples before the Congress of Vienna, as if the Congress had been called to restore order after the 1848 revolutions. It was the other way round: the Congress met in 1814-1815, and the revolutions of 1848 were uprisings against the conservative order it had created.
distractorRationale.c: This list puts the Congress of Vienna before the storming of the Bastille. The Congress dealt with the aftermath of the Napoleonic Wars, which grew out of the French Revolution, so it cannot come before the Revolution began in 1789.
distractorRationale.a: This list puts the German Empire before the Springtime of Peoples. In 1848-1849 the Frankfurt Parliament tried and failed to unite Germany; unification came only in 1871, after the Franco-Prussian War.
distractorRationale.b: This list opens with the Springtime of Peoples, treating the 1848 revolutions as a forerunner of the French Revolution. They came almost sixty years after 1789 and were partly inspired by its ideals.

accessibilityText: Four events are listed: the Congress of Vienna at the end of the Napoleonic Wars; the proclamation of the German Empire in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles; the storming of the Bastille in Paris; and the wave of revolutions known as the Springtime of Peoples. The question asks which list orders them from earliest to latest. The five choices are: Bastille, Congress of Vienna, German Empire, Springtime of Peoples; Springtime of Peoples, Bastille, Congress of Vienna, German Empire; Congress of Vienna, Bastille, Springtime of Peoples, German Empire; Bastille, Springtime of Peoples, Congress of Vienna, German Empire; and Bastille, Congress of Vienna, Springtime of Peoples, German Empire.

A swaps the last two, and D swaps the middle two.
